title: Coefficient estimation accuracy
statement: Let a deterministic Goldreich–Levin input have dimension $n>0$, rational accuracy $a/b$ with $a>0$ and $2a\le b$, and Fourier bound $B\ge1$, and put $\varepsilon=a/b$. Let $f$ be a Boolean function on $n$ sign-valued coordinates with Fourier $1$-norm at most $B$. For a nonempty finite family $\mathcal F$ of coordinate subsets, assume $|\mathcal F|\le\lceil4/\tau^2\rceil$, where $M=\max(1,\lceil4B^2/\varepsilon\rceil)$ and $\tau=\varepsilon/(4M)$. For every $U\in\mathcal F$, the rational sample estimate of the Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $U$ differs from that coefficient by at most $\varepsilon/(2|\mathcal F|)$.
hypotheses_covered: Twice the accuracy numerator is at most its denominator
Fourier bound is at least one
Target Fourier 1-norm is at most the Fourier bound
Family of coordinate subsets is nonempty
Family size is at most the active cap
